summary.text: Take \(n=7\). Since every permitted value of \(x\) is at least \(3\), the ordering \(x\le y\le z\) forces \(x+y+z\ge 9\), contradicting the required sum \(x+y+z=7\).

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
a(n)=\#\bigl\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}^3:
 x\le y\le z,\ x+y+z=n,
\]
\[
2x-1,\ 2y-1,\ 2z-1,\ 2xy-1,\ 2xz-1,\ 2yz-1
\text{ are all prime}\bigr\}.
\]
The conjecture asserts two things simultaneously for every integer \(n\): first, if \(n>5\), then \(a(n)>0\); and second, if \(n>6\), then there is such a positive ordered representation
\[
n=x+y+z,\qquad x\le y\le z,
\]
in which
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\}.
\]
(The phrase “such a representation” includes the positivity, ordering, and six primality conditions from the definition.)

We disprove the universal assertion by taking
\[
n=7.
\]
Certainly \(7>6\). Therefore, if the conjecture were true, its second, “moreover” clause would provide positive integers \(x,y,z\) satisfying
\[
x+y+z=7,\qquad x\le y\le z,
\]
and
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\},
\]
as well as the six stated primality conditions.

Membership in the displayed finite set leaves the five cases
\[
x=3,\quad x=4,\quad x=6,\quad x=10,\quad x=15.
\]
In every case, \(x\ge 3\). Because \(x\le y\le z\), it follows that
\[
y\ge x\ge 3\qquad\text{and}\qquad z\ge y\ge x\ge 3.
\]
Consequently,
\[
x+y+z\ge 3+3+3=9.
\]
This contradicts the required equation \(x+y+z=7\).

Equivalently, one may see the contradiction in each of the five possible cases directly. If \(x=3\), ordering gives \(x+y+z\ge 9\); if \(x=4\), it gives \(x+y+z\ge 12\); for \(x=6,10,15\), it gives the respective lower bounds \(18,30,45\). None can equal \(7\).

Thus no positive ordered triple summing to \(7\) can have its least entry \(x\) in \(\{3,4,6,10,15\}\). This obstruction occurs before any primality condition is considered, so the primality requirements cannot rescue the representation. Hence the “moreover” clause is false at \(n=7\). Since the conjecture requires both clauses for every \(n\), failure of this clause at a single value disproves the entire conjecture.
